steps.body:
Tangent has its own formula, all tangents:

tan(A ± B) = (tan A ± tan B) / (1 ∓ tan A tan B).

The denominator's sign is OPPOSITE the numerator's. For tan 75° = tan(45° + 30°): (1 + 1/√3)/(1 − 1·1/√3), which simplifies to **2 + √3 ≈ 3.732**.

predict.prompt: Cofunction claims survive any θ — even past 90°, where the “co” angle goes negative?

options.label: They hold everywhere — the swap needs no quadrant escort
Only while both angles stay acute

predict.reveal: Everywhere. Drag θ through 90° and beyond: the swapped-coordinate point never leaves the direct one, negative co-angle and all. The quadrant-blind version — tacking on a sign — detaches immediately. Identities don't check quadrants; wrong formulas do.

widget.prompt: Direct point at 90° − θ. Pick the cofunction formula that stays glued even when θ passes 90°, then land on 115° — past the crossing.

ghostChoices.label: (sin θ, −cos θ) — “adjust for the quadrant”
ghostChoices.feedback: The adjustment IS the error: past 90°, cos θ is already negative, and negating it again mirrors the point away. The plain swap carries its own signs — watch it hold while this one detaches at the crossing.

widget.successFeedback: Still glued at 115° — the swap survived the crossing because cos θ turned negative on its own, exactly as the co-angle 90° − 115° = −25° demands. Tangent's sum rule inherits this same discipline in its denominator: signs ride inside the functions, never alongside them.
widget.lowFeedback: Formula's right — keep dragging through 90° to 115° and watch the crossing change nothing.
widget.highFeedback: Past 115° — back up; the point of interest is just past the crossing.

explanationVariants: tan 75° is steep — near the 90° wall — so a large value ≈ 3.73 is expected.

commonErrors.feedback: 1.577 forgets to divide by the (small) denominator 1 − 1/√3 ≈ 0.42. The full value is 2 + √3 ≈ 3.732.
0.268 ≈ tan 15° — you may have inverted. tan 75° = 2 + √3 ≈ 3.732.

steps.body: **Cofunctions**: sin and cos are the SAME wave a quarter-turn apart (recall cos x = sin(x + π/2)), which means **sin(90° − θ) = cos θ** and cos(90° − θ) = sin θ. 'Co' literally means *complementary*: each function of an angle equals its cofunction of the complement.

explanationVariants: The complement of 34° is 56°; cosine of an angle is sine of its complement.

widget.prompt: cos 34° equals sin of which angle?

options.feedback: Right — 90° − 34° = 56°, and cos θ = sin(90° − θ).
sin 34° ≠ cos 34° (unless θ = 45°). The cofunction uses the COMPLEMENT: 56°.
That's the supplement, not the complement. Cofunctions use 90° − θ = 56°.

explanationVariants: sin(90° − θ) = sin90°cosθ − cos90°sinθ = 1·cosθ − 0·sinθ = cos θ — the sum formula PROVES the cofunction identity.
With sin90° = 1 and cos90° = 0, the difference formula collapses to cos θ.

widget.prompt: Expanding sin(90° − θ) with the difference formula gives:

options.label: cos θ — sin 90° = 1 survives; cos 90° = 0 vanishes.
options.feedback: Right — the formula collapses: 1·cosθ − 0·sinθ = cos θ, proving the cofunction identity.

options.label: sin θ, if the cofunction relation is reversed.
options.feedback: Check the constants: sin90° = 1 multiplies cos θ, and cos90° = 0 kills the sin θ term. Result: cos θ.

options.label: 1 − sin θ, if the subtraction formula is misread.
options.feedback: The formula is a difference of PRODUCTS, not of terms: 1·cosθ − 0·sinθ = cos θ.

explanationVariants: The difference flips both signs: numerator minus, denominator plus. 2 − √3 ≈ 0.27.

takeaways: tan(A ± B) = (tanA ± tanB)/(1 ∓ tanA tanB) — denominator sign opposite.
Cofunction: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.
The sum formulas PROVE the cofunction identities.

concept.body: tan(A±B): numerator tanA±tanB, denominator 1∓tanA tanB (opposite sign). Cofunction: any function of θ equals its co-partner of (90°−θ).
